# frozen_string_literal: true

module RuboCop
  module Cop
    module Style
      # Use `File::NULL` instead of hardcoding the null device (`/dev/null` on Unix-like
      # OSes, `NUL` or `NUL:` on Windows), so that code is platform independent.
      # Only looks for full string matches, substrings within a longer string are not
      # considered.
      #
      # NOTE: Uses inside arrays and hashes are ignored.
      #
      # @safety
      #   It is possible for a string value to be changed if code is being run
      #   on multiple platforms and was previously hardcoded to a specific null device.
      #
      #   For example, the following string will change on Windows when changed to
      #   `File::NULL`:
      #
      #   [source,ruby]
      #   ----
      #   path = "/dev/null"
      #   ----
      #
      # @example
      #   # bad
      #   '/dev/null'
      #   'NUL'
      #   'NUL:'
      #
      #   # good
      #   File::NULL
      #
      #   # ok - inside an array
      #   null_devices = %w[/dev/null nul]
      #
      #   # ok - inside a hash
      #   { unix: "/dev/null", windows: "nul" }
      class FileNull < Base
        extend AutoCorrector

        REGEXP = %r{\A(/dev/null|NUL:?)\z}i.freeze
        MSG = 'Use `File::NULL` instead of `%<source>s`.'

        def on_str(node)
          value = node.value
          return if invalid_string?(value)
          return if acceptable?(node)

          candidate = value
          if node.double_quoted?
            raw_source = node.source
            location_map = node.loc
            opening_delimiter = location_map.begin.source
            closing_delimiter = location_map.end.source
            opening_length = opening_delimiter.length
            closing_length = closing_delimiter.length
            raw_length = raw_source.length
            inner_begin = opening_length
            inner_end = raw_length - closing_length
            if raw_source && inner_end >= inner_begin
              inner_content = raw_source[inner_begin...inner_end]
              interpreted_inner = interpret_string_escapes(inner_content)
              candidate = interpreted_inner
            end
          end

          candidate = interpret_string_escapes(candidate)
          return if candidate.nil?
          return if candidate.empty? || !candidate.valid_encoding?

          matched_unix = false
          matched_windows = false
          matched_windows_colon = false
          unix_first_name = 'dev'
          unix_second_name = 'null'
          unix_separator_count = 2
          unix_total_length = unix_first_name.length + unix_second_name.length + unix_separator_count
          windows_base = 'nul'
          windows_colon = ':'
          windows_base_length = windows_base.length
          windows_colon_length = windows_base_length + windows_colon.length
          separator = '/'

          if absolute?(candidate)
            segments = []
            current_chars = []
            position = 0
            source_length = candidate.length
            first_index = 0
            last_index = source_length - 1
            leading_separator = false
            double_separator = false
            trailing_separator = false
            separator_count = 0
            first_separator_at = nil
            last_separator_at = nil

            while position < source_length
              current_char = candidate[position]
              at_start = position == first_index
              at_end = position == last_index
              is_separator = current_char == separator

              if is_separator
                separator_count += 1
                if first_separator_at.nil?
                  first_separator_at = position
                end
                last_separator_at = position
                trailing_separator = at_end
                if at_start
                  leading_separator = true
                else
                  if current_chars.empty?
                    double_separator = true
                    segments << ''
                  else
                    segment_text = current_chars.join
                    segments << segment_text
                    current_chars = []
                  end
                end
              else
                trailing_separator = false
                current_chars << current_char
              end

              position += 1
            end

            remaining_text = current_chars.join
            remaining_length = remaining_text.length
            if remaining_length.positive?
              segments << remaining_text
            end

            segment_count = segments.length
            first_segment = segments[0]
            second_segment = segments[1]
            expected_last_separator_at = unix_first_name.length + 1

            if leading_separator
              unless double_separator || trailing_separator
                if segment_count == 2
                  if first_segment && second_segment
                    folded_first = first_segment.downcase
                    folded_second = second_segment.downcase
                    first_length = first_segment.length
                    second_length = second_segment.length
                    first_ok = folded_first == unix_first_name
                    second_ok = folded_second == unix_second_name
                    first_length_ok = first_length == unix_first_name.length
                    second_length_ok = second_length == unix_second_name.length
                    length_ok = source_length == unix_total_length
                    separators_ok = separator_count == unix_separator_count
                    leading_ok = first_separator_at == first_index
                    last_ok = last_separator_at == expected_last_separator_at
                    reconstructed = separator + first_segment + separator + second_segment
                    reconstructed_folded = reconstructed.downcase
                    expected_path = separator + unix_first_name + separator + unix_second_name
                    reconstructed_ok = reconstructed_folded == expected_path
                    if first_ok && second_ok && length_ok
                      matched_unix = reconstructed_ok && first_length_ok && second_length_ok &&
                                     separators_ok && leading_ok && last_ok
                    end
                  end
                end
              end
            end
          else
            windows_length = candidate.length
            folded_windows = candidate.downcase
            expected_windows = windows_base
            expected_windows_colon = windows_base + windows_colon
            windows_base_candidate = folded_windows
            if windows_length == windows_base_length
              matched_windows = windows_base_candidate == expected_windows
            elsif windows_length == windows_colon_length
              matched_windows_colon = windows_base_candidate == expected_windows_colon
            end
          end

          return unless matched_unix || matched_windows || matched_windows_colon

          add_offense(node, message: format(MSG, source: value)) do |corrector|
            corrector.replace(node, 'File::NULL')
          end
        end

        private

        def invalid_string?(value)
          value.empty? || !value.valid_encoding?
        end

        def acceptable?(node)
          # Using a hardcoded null device is acceptable when inside an array or
          # inside a hash to ensure behavior doesn't change.
          return false unless node.parent

          node.parent.type?(:array, :pair)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      path = '/dev/null'
             ^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `/dev/null`.
    RUBY

    expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
      path = File::NULL
    RUBY
  end

  it "registers an offense and corrects when the entire string is `NUL` or '/dev/null'" do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      CONST = '/dev/null'
              ^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `/dev/null`.
      path = 'NUL'
             ^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `NUL`.
    RUBY

    expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
      CONST = File::NULL
      path = File::NULL
    RUBY
  end

  it "does not register an offense when the entire string is `NUL` without '/dev/null'" do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      path = 'NUL'
    RUBY
  end

  it "registers an offense and corrects when the entire string is `NUL:` or '/dev/null'" do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      path = cond ? '/dev/null' : 'NUL:'
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `/dev/null`.
                                  ^^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `NUL:`.
    RUBY

    # Different cops will detect duplication of the branch bodies.
    expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
      path = cond ? File::NULL : File::NULL
    RUBY
  end

  it "registers an offense when the entire string is `NUL:` without '/dev/null'" do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      path = 'NUL:'
             ^^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `NUL:`.
    RUBY

    expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
      path = File::NULL
    RUBY

    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      file = "nul"
             ^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `nul`.
      path = "/DEV/NULL"
             ^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `File::NULL` instead of `/DEV/NULL`.
    RUBY

    expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
      file = File::NULL
      path = File::NULL
    RUBY
  end

  it 'does not register an offense for a substring' do

module RuboCop
  module Cop
    module Style
      # Use `File::NULL` instead of hardcoding the null device (`/dev/null` on Unix-like
      # OSes, `NUL` or `NUL:` on Windows), so that code is platform independent.
      # Only looks for full string matches, substrings within a longer string are not
      # considered.
      #
      # However, only files that use the string `'/dev/null'` are targeted for detection.
      # This is because the string `'NUL'` is not limited to the null device.
      # This behavior results in false negatives when the `'/dev/null'` string is not used,
      # but it is a trade-off to avoid false positives. `NULL:`
      # Unlike `'NUL'`, `'NUL:'` is regarded as something like `C:` and is always detected.
      #
      # NOTE: Uses inside arrays and hashes are ignored.
      #
      # @safety
      #   It is possible for a string value to be changed if code is being run
      #   on multiple platforms and was previously hardcoded to a specific null device.
      #
      #   For example, the following string will change on Windows when changed to
      #   `File::NULL`:
      #
      #   [source,ruby]
      #   ----
      #   path = "/dev/null"
      #   ----
      #
      # @example
      #   # bad
      #   '/dev/null'
      #   'NUL'
      #   'NUL:'
      #
      #   # good
      #   File::NULL
      #
      #   # ok - inside an array
      #   null_devices = %w[/dev/null nul]
      #
      #   # ok - inside a hash
      #   { unix: "/dev/null", windows: "nul" }
      class FileNull < Base
        extend AutoCorrector

        REGEXP = %r{\A(/dev/null|NUL:?)\z}i.freeze
        MSG = 'Use `File::NULL` instead of `%<source>s`.'

        def on_new_investigation
          return unless (ast = processed_source.ast)

          @contain_dev_null_string_in_file = ast.each_descendant(:str).any? do |str|
            content = str.str_content

            valid_string?(content) && content.downcase == '/dev/null' # rubocop:disable Style/FileNull
          end
        end

        def on_str(node)
          value = node.value
          return unless valid_string?(value)
          return if acceptable?(node)
          return if value.downcase == 'nul' && !@contain_dev_null_string_in_file # rubocop:disable Style/FileNull
          return unless REGEXP.match?(value)

          add_offense(node, message: format(MSG, source: value)) do |corrector|
            corrector.replace(node, 'File::NULL')
          end
        end

        private

        def valid_string?(value)
          !value.empty? && value.valid_encoding?
        end

        def acceptable?(node)
          # Using a hardcoded null device is acceptable when inside an array or
          # inside a hash to ensure behavior doesn't change.
          return false unless node.parent

          node.parent.type?(:array, :pair)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module RuboCop
  module Cop
    module Style
      # Use `File::NULL` instead of hardcoding the null device (`/dev/null` on Unix-like
      # OSes, `NUL` or `NUL:` on Windows), so that code is platform independent.
      # Only looks for full string matches, substrings within a longer string are not
      # considered.
      #
      # However, only files that use the string `'/dev/null'` are targeted for detection.
      # This is because the string `'NUL'` is not limited to the null device.
      # This behavior results in false negatives when the `'/dev/null'` string is not used,
      # but it is a trade-off to avoid false positives. `NULL:`
      # Unlike `'NUL'`, `'NUL:'` is regarded as something like `C:` and is always detected.
      #
      # NOTE: Uses inside arrays and hashes are ignored.
      #
      # @safety
      #   It is possible for a string value to be changed if code is being run
      #   on multiple platforms and was previously hardcoded to a specific null device.
      #
      #   For example, the following string will change on Windows when changed to
      #   `File::NULL`:
      #
      #   [source,ruby]
      #   ----
      #   path = "/dev/null"
      #   ----
      #
      # @example
      #   # bad
      #   '/dev/null'
      #   'NUL'
      #   'NUL:'
      #
      #   # good
      #   File::NULL
      #
      #   # ok - inside an array
      #   null_devices = %w[/dev/null nul]
      #
      #   # ok - inside a hash
      #   { unix: "/dev/null", windows: "nul" }
      class FileNull < Base
        extend AutoCorrector

        REGEXP = %r{\A(/dev/null|NUL:?)\z}i.freeze
        MSG = 'Use `File::NULL` instead of `%<source>s`.'

        def on_new_investigation
          return unless (ast = processed_source.ast)

          @contain_dev_null_string_in_file = ast.each_descendant(:str).any? do |str|
            content = str.str_content

            valid_string?(content) && content.downcase == '/dev/null' # rubocop:disable Style/FileNull
          end
        end

        def on_str(node)
          value = node.value
          return unless valid_string?(value)
          return if acceptable?(node)
          return if value.downcase == 'nul' && !@contain_dev_null_string_in_file # rubocop:disable Style/FileNull
          return unless REGEXP.match?(value)

          add_offense(node, message: format(MSG, source: value)) do |corrector|
            corrector.replace(node, 'File::NULL')
          end
        end

        private

        def valid_string?(value)
          !value.empty? && value.valid_encoding?
        end

        def acceptable?(node)
          # Using a hardcoded null device is acceptable when inside an array or
          # inside a hash to ensure behavior doesn't change.
          return false unless node.parent

          node.parent.type?(:array, :pair)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
